stories.title: Fail closed on blob integrity checks at every materialization path
stories.scope: R2 asset tier read path. Build one verified-materialization chokepoint in the tier's module (`platform/src/assets.ts`, or the module the first-slice row `r2-asset-tier-manifest-format` lands — conform, never fork the format): `readVerifiedBlob(env, blobId, expectedSha256)` fetches the object via the asset-bucket R2 binding (name pinned by the first slice; wired in `platform/wrangler.jsonc`, typed bindings regenerated with `wrangler types` into `platform/worker-configuration.d.ts`), recomputes SHA-256 over the exact bytes, and returns them only when the digest equals both the content-addressed blob id and the pointer's recorded content hash. Mismatch — tampered object, substituted key, or pointer/content divergence — throws a typed `BlobIntegrityError` and materializes nothing. Every site that can return blob bytes must call the chokepoint: the asset download route in `platform/src/index.ts`, any clone/checkout materialization hook, and future presigned-confirmation paths; no byte-returning `bucket.get(...)` exists outside it. Route boundary maps the error to a non-2xx `{ok:false,error:"integrity"}` body per the tier's contract (bump `platform/CONTRACT.md` first when a new route/response shape lands — contract-first, FR-42). No partial content, no fallback to another object/key, never cache or serve unverified bytes; log the mismatch with pointer path and expected/actual digest only (no blob content; AD-4 / NFR-5).
stories.acceptance: Given a stored blob whose bytes hash to H and a pointer recording content hash H, when a read materializes it, then the exact bytes are returned. Given a stored object whose bytes no longer hash to the pointer's content hash (or to its content-addressed key) after tampering or substitution, when any read path materializes it, then the read fails closed: `BlobIntegrityError` at the module boundary and a non-2xx `{ok:false,error:"integrity"}` at the route — zero bytes returned, no silent substitution, no fallback. Both mismatch directions are covered by tests: pointer hash != stored digest, and blob id key != stored digest. The source tree has exactly one byte-returning read of the asset bucket (the chokepoint; grep-verified) and the test drives both the module and the route handler through it. The mismatch log line contains no blob content.
stories.notes: Dedupe: store, binding and pointer format are owned by the existing pending row `r2-asset-tier-manifest-format`; this story authors only the delta — the verified read chokepoint and the fail-closed semantics of FR-47 consequence 2 ('a blob whose content hash does not match its pointer fails closed ... verification runs on any read path that materializes a blob'). Distinct from pending row `write-chunk-manifests-and-merkle-integrity-into-repo` (chunk/Merkle reconstruction inside the repo — a different mechanism, not duplicated here). Story ids are lowercased to satisfy the compile lint slug regex (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,59}$`); same titles keep the same ids on re-compile.

stories.title: Delete asset pointers lifecycle-safely with bucket rules and no orphan blobs
stories.scope: Lifecycle half of the tier. (1) Bucket lifecycle rules: commit the asset bucket's retention/expiry configuration as `platform/r2-lifecycle.json` and apply it with the lockfile-pinned wrangler (`cd platform && ./node_modules/.bin/wrangler r2 bucket lifecycle set <asset-bucket> r2-lifecycle.json`); `wrangler r2 bucket lifecycle list <asset-bucket>` must show the committed rules; record the bucket name plus apply command in the platform tier doc/README when the first slice pins the bucket. (2) Reference-aware, lifecycle-safe deletes: a repo path removal is a normal file delete (the pointer disappears with the commit/fold). After the platform's write path (`/land` in `platform/src/land.ts` + `platform/src/index.ts`) folds removals, each removed pointer's blob is checked against the union of every repo's pointer manifests (Artifacts listing; source of truth is the repo manifests — any cache/index must be rebuildable from them) and is deleted/scheduled only when its reference count is zero. Shared blobs are never deleted while any repo or path still references them. Per-request work stays inside the 30 s CPU envelope (NFR-1): the land path checks only blobs touched by the fold; bulk reclamation is out-of-band. (3) Orphan audit + sweep: `platform/scripts/r2-orphan-sweep.mjs` lists bucket keys, subtracts the union of manifest-referenced blob ids across all repos, reports orphans, deletes those older than a grace window, and exits non-zero if any orphan remains after the sweep; it runs from the repo root using the same API-token resolution as `platform/scripts/fanout.mjs`.
stories.acceptance: Given manifests where path a points to blobX and no other repo or path references blobX, when path a is removed through the normal commit/fold path, then the pointer is gone and blobX is scheduled/deleted (reference count zero). Given blobX is still referenced from another repo or path, when a is removed, then blobX survives — no shared-blob deletion. Given a bucket containing an unreferenced blob older than the grace window, when the sweep runs, then it deletes it and a follow-up audit reports zero orphans; a fresh unreferenced blob inside the grace window is reported but not deleted. Given the deployed asset bucket, when `wrangler r2 bucket lifecycle list` runs, then the committed retention/expiry rules are present. No request path performs an unbounded bucket scan (NFR-1).
stories.notes: Dedupe: storage/binding/format are owned by pending `r2-asset-tier-manifest-format`; big-binary routing is owned by pending `split-storage-source-in-artifacts-big-binaries-in-r2`; this story authors only the delta — bucket lifecycle rules, reference-aware delete scheduling after removal, and the orphan audit (FR-47 consequence 3: 'removing a path removes the pointer and schedules the blob; no orphan-blob accumulation'). Pending `add-binary-delta-encoding-for-archive-like-assets` is a game-pipeline performance item and is not duplicated. The sweep is an out-of-band script because bucket-wide scans cannot fit the 30 s Worker CPU envelope.

stories.title: Keep clone, change-set, and fork-point reads unchanged for asset pointers
stories.scope: Read-surface invariance for the pointer layer (AD-10: the merge/conflict/diff layer operates on Artifacts, never on R2 blobs; FR-47 consequences 1 and 4). (a) No git path reads R2: clone/checkout and change-set computation in `platform/src/githttp.ts`, `platform/src/memfs.ts`, `platform/src/land.ts` and the `/changes` + `/proposals` handlers in `platform/src/index.ts` never fetch blobs — pointer files are ordinary repo files carrying (path, blob id, content hash, size) per the pinned format; prove it with an instrumented bucket stub that fails the test on any blob read during git operations. (b) Fork-point computation is unchanged: the most recent shared first-parent commit vs base, walk limit 200, base-head fallback (CONTRACT.md:52/54; SPINE:75) selects the same commit for the same histories with pointers present; extract the walk into a testable helper if it is currently inline. (c) Change-sets containing only pointer edits render as file rows (path/status/action) with no blob access; the non-diffable metadata-only pointer rendering conforms to the shape the first slice pinned (`r2-asset-tier-manifest-format` owns the format and the baseline rendering — complete gaps only, never redesign). Response-shape changes go through `platform/CONTRACT.md` first (FR-42).
stories.acceptance: Given a scratch repo pair (fork of base) carrying an asset pointer file, when cloned/checked out, then the pointer file is byte-identical and the instrumented bucket records zero blob reads. Given identical repo histories, when fork-point selection runs with and without pointer files in the trees, then the selected ancestor commit is identical (first-parent walk limit 200 and base-head fallback preserved). Given a proposal whose change-set contains only pointer edits, then `GET /changes` and `GET /proposals` render the file rows without fetching blob content, with the pinned metadata-only pointer fields present, and the change-set stats and fork point are unchanged versus the same tree without pointers. Any response-shape change is present in `platform/CONTRACT.md` before the code lands.
stories.notes: Dedupe: the pointer format and the baseline metadata-only rendering are owned by pending `r2-asset-tier-manifest-format` (its round-trip check covers pointer visibility in /changes); this story authors the invariance delta — zero blob reads from any git path, unchanged fork-point walk/fallback, and no change-set stats drift (FR-47 consequence 1: 'clones, change-sets, and the fork-point contract are unchanged'). Write-surface invariance is covered by `e12-impl-land-mask-invariance` — no overlap.

stories.title: Prove landing, masking, and fork-point contracts unchanged with asset pointers
stories.scope: Write-surface invariance (FR-47 consequence 4: 'the five landing semantics, secret masking, and the fork-point change-set contract are unchanged — the tier adds a pointer layer only'). Extend the scratch-only live-probe pattern of `porting/tests/land-hardening.probe.mjs` into `porting/tests/r2-land-invariance.probe.mjs`: REST-fork scratch repos only (never `demo` or `agent-1..4`), commit an asset pointer file plus a second change, and assert the pinned landing contract end-to-end against the deployed worker: 200 `{landed, evidence{repos,commit,ancestor,heads,foldHash}}` with base-ref equality; `409 stale` (reviewed baseHead/heads mismatch — CONTRACT.md:89-90); `409 withheld-secret` for a secret-class pointer path with values absent from every body (CONTRACT.md:78, masking law CONTRACT.md:175-179); `409 conflict`; `409 no-changes`; `409 base-moved` on concurrent double-land — in the pinned precondition order 400 -> 429 -> 403 -> 409 stale -> 409 withheld-secret -> 409 conflict -> 409 no-changes -> 409 base-moved -> 200 (CONTRACT.md:104). Masking: a credential-adjacent pointer value follows AD-4/AD-10 — key names only; assert the value is absent from every response body and from the worker log tail the probe observes. Fork-point contract: `evidence.ancestor[repo]` equals the fork-point commit for asset-bearing repos exactly as for pointer-free controls (CONTRACT.md:54). Wire only what is missing so pointers ride the ordinary fold/mask paths — landing mechanics are owned by the land-hardening rows; no rebuild.
stories.acceptance: On the deployed worker, the scratch-only probe with asset-pointer fixtures exits 0 having asserted: 200 landed with evidence fields and base-ref equality; all five 409 semantics (stale, withheld-secret, conflict, no-changes, base-moved) with the pinned status and error text; secret-class pointer path yields 409 withheld-secret with key names only and the pointer value never appears in any response body or observed log; `evidence.ancestor` equals the fork-point commit with pointers identical to the pointer-free control. The probe creates and deletes only its own scratch repos and exits non-zero on any violation.
stories.notes: Dedupe: landing mechanics and hardening are owned by existing rows (`land-hardening` [pending], `cpu-budget-hardening-large-change-sets-within-the-30s-worker` [pending]) — this story authors only the pointer-layer invariance probe (five 409 semantics + 200, masking, ancestor), no rebuild. Read-surface invariance is `e12-impl-git-surfaces-unchanged-pointers` — no overlap. Probe commits only its own scratch repos and never lands into `demo`.
